title: The Compass of Truth, or Risala-i-Haq-Numa
author: Muhammad Dara Shikoh (1615-1659)
edition_cited: Panini Office, Allahabad, 1912; Digital Library of India scan, archive.org in.ernet.dli.2015.102305 (OCR text, some garbling)
tradition: Qadiri (Mian Mir / Mulla Shah lineage), Mughal India
locator_hints: Ch. on the plane of Nasut / 'Method of meditation': close the eyes, fix attention on the heart, see the Master's picture (OCR line ~392-412)
Three centres of the heart, incl. the 'colourless' spherical heart (lines ~405-460, 927)
Alam-i-misal / Malakut: 'the picture of the form, which is seen after closing the eyes' (lines ~538-590)
Regulation of breath with the fingers closing ears, eyes, lips and nostrils; effects incl. 'subtle illumination' (lines ~800-950)
Sultan-ul-azkar, practised in a cave or at night; mainly inner sound (lines ~1035-1270)
Later chapter: both eyes closed, plane of no colour (lines ~1350-1370)
summary: A short practical manual in four 'planes' (Nasut, Malakut, Jabarut, Lahut) by the Mughal prince, written for seekers without a teacher. It tells the practitioner to sit alone, close the eyes, fix attention on the heart and see the form of the Master there; says the form seen after closing the eyes belongs to the 'alam-i mithal and that with practice the mirror of the heart brightens and forms of prophets and saints appear. It then gives a detailed breath-retention exercise with the fingers sealing ears, eyes, lips and nostrils (eyes shut by the index fingers 'but the fingers should not press the eye-balls'), and reports heat, buoyancy and 'a subtle illumination in thy heart, and in all thy body'. The Sultan-ul-azkar section concerns inner sound more than light. The translator's theosophical notes are interleaved.
why_relevant: Explicit step-by-step sense-closure and breath-retention instruction with a claimed result of forms and illumination seen with closed eyes; seed lead confirmed. Whether 'illumination' is visual needs the reading agent's judgement.

date_evidence.basis: archive.org metadata date 1912 for the DLI scan; title page gives composition 1055-1056 AH
